questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving at the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not speed up or brake. Keep your speed the same so the other vehicle can safely pass you and move back into your lane.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can harm your ability to drive safely. It affects your judgment and your physical control of the vehicle. Even small amounts of alcohol can lead to criminal charges if you drive.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under ride in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Children age 12 and under should always ride in the back seat. Airbags can be dangerous for children and do not provide safe protection for them.

questions.question: Which habit is dangerous when driving through work zones?

options.text: Following other vehicles too closely.
Not paying attention to workers and equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and moving equipment.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Turn around and find another route.
Drive slowly through the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded water. Water may hide dangers you cannot see. Always turn around and find a different route to your destination.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Relax and focus on your driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow closely behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and focus on your driving.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and concentrate on driving safely. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Follow speed limits and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending ahead.
A divided highway is beginning ahead.
The road will be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is beginning ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right of the center divider.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones. Drive carefully when you see orange warning signs or equipment on the road.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. How do you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to stay at a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in rainy weather to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast causes your tires to lose contact with the road and makes it hard to control your vehicle.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. Always make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you try to pass the car in front of you.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for vehicles in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop. Look for traffic in all directions before you go.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using just one part gives you much less protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle the lap belt.

questions.question: A distraction when driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to take sudden action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your focus away from driving. Distractions can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, watch your rearview mirror. You can only safely return to your original lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt. Secure any items in your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while moving.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not following traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not following traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system. Eating, drinking caffeine, or anything else cannot speed this up.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your safety belt and check that all passengers have buckled theirs.

questions.question: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a thin layer of water instead of the road. To prevent hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Reduce your speed on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When it is dawn, dusk, rainy, or snowy, it is hard to see and be seen. What should you turn on to let other drivers know you are there?

options.text: The dashboard lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not be able to see you. Turn on your low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Position your vehicle parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle ahead is turning left.
When there are two or more lanes going in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You may never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used for what purpose?

options.text: To make drivers frustrated about slow traffic.
To inconvenience drivers.
To keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. When you approach a work zone, watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and guide your direction.

questions.question: What should you do before backing your vehicle?

options.text: Walk around the vehicle to make sure nothing and no one is behind it.
Rev your engine.
Flash your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the vehicle to make sure nothing and no one is behind it.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk completely around your vehicle to check for people or obstacles behind it. Look over your shoulder and out the rear window when backing. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains cross first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains cross first.
questions.explanation: A round sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing. This sign is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what should you use to help others see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: As daylight fades, turn on your low beam headlights to help others see you. Only use your high beam headlights in open areas where no other drivers are present.

questions.question: What is the best way to change from one lane to another?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Change lanes only when necessary. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that there is an intersection with a side road ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake suddenly to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops gradually and smoothly.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park completely off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park completely off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, park all four wheels off the road if you can.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Keep your normal speed.
Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.
When there is a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a red traffic light. Always obey police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and cautious. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: If you must stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the first passing car.
Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of an interstate, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. Walking on an interstate is very dangerous.

questions.question: On a slippery road, keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Longer than normal.
Shorter than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Longer than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road. Leave a bigger gap between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
Half the width of a lane.
The same full lane width as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the entire lane width just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: As alcohol in your blood increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you become.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle moving in the same direction, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:

options.text: About three seconds have passed.
You can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before moving back. Always check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
questions.explanation: You must obey flaggers at construction sites. They direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make driving unsafe. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough and cold medicines, allergy medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Do not stay beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: Night driving is difficult because:

options.text: Speed limits are higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, poor visibility makes it hard to judge how far away vehicles are and how fast they are moving. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Paying attention to the road and staying focused.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Always drive within speed limits and adjust your speed for weather and traffic.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
Do not have to follow any rules of the road.
Must always give way to motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as cars. Drivers must respect bicyclists' rights on the road.

questions.question: In a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: Roundabouts flow counterclockwise around a center island. Entering drivers must yield to traffic already in the roundabout, follow the circle to the right, and exit onto their street.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has curves.
